shared_elements: upright rectangular stone slab/pillar carved in low relief
profile-view figures (animal heads in A, human head in B)
band/row of repeated small rectangular compartments
carved arm/hand and elongated linear object held or extended
flat, outlined relief on pale tan stone
division of the surface into registers or panels
justification: Both are upright tan stone slabs carved in shallow, flat relief and both subdivide their surfaces, most specifically through a run of repeated small rectangular compartments (a horizontal hatched band in A, vertical stacked blocks in B) set beside larger profile figures. The decisive difference is subject and organisation: A is a register-stacked bestiary of schematic animals with no dominant figure, whereas B is dominated by a single large, elaborately costumed standing human in profile framed by inscription-like panels, rendered with far more modelling and detail.
